title: Entropy-aware microstride concentrator for sequence-length consolidation
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description:
Goal: Implement an entropy-aware microstride concentrator that dynamically groups incoming requests into compact micro-batches based on per-request token-entropy and sequence-length microstrides, reducing padding waste while preserving latency SLOs. The feature combines a lightweight entropy estimator, run-length microstride bucketing, and kernel hinting to pick specialized attention kernels (packed vs. dense) at micro-batch dispatch time.

Background: Current bucketizers group primarily by sequence length histograms which leaves residual padding when request lengths are multimodal or when prefill/decode interleaving produces fragmented sequences. This ticket explores an orthogonal signal: token-level entropy and microstride patterns (clusters of short/long segments within a request) to better coalesce requests that will benefit from the same kernel and attention sparsity strategy.

Approach:
- Entropy estimator: sample the first N tokens of each request and compute a lightweight entropy score using log-prob approximations from the scoring model or from cached prefix stats. Entropy is represented as a discrete bucket (low/med/high).
- Microstride signature: compute a 2-bit stride pattern for the prefill portion (short-run/long-run) to capture intra-request length variability.
- Concentrator algorithm: combine sequence-length quantile, entropy bucket, and microstride signature into a micro-batch key. Maintain per-worker micro-batch windows with timeout heuristics to meet latency SLOs.
- Kernel hinting: when a micro-batch forms, emit kernel selection hints to the runtime (e.g., use packed-attention optimized kernel when low-entropy short-filled batches exceed threshold; otherwise use dense attention kernel).
- Prefill/decode scheduling: prioritize prefill consolidation of similar entropy/signature requests and schedule decode tokens to avoid fragmenting micro-batches. Use soft-prioritization: do not violate latency SLO > 99th pct.

Acceptance criteria:
- Median tokens padded per-batch reduced by >= 28% on web-chat workload (compared to baseline histogram bucketing).
- 95th percentile latency change <= +5ms for P99 SLOs under 95% load, or improved if possible.
- End-to-end cost per token decreases by >= 12% in benchmark suite.
- No regressions on correctness/regression tests; all unit + integration tests passing in CI.

Performance experiments summary: initial A/B on synthetic multimodal length trace (mix of 24, 128, 512 seqs) shows padded tokens reduced by 32% and average GPU utilization increase of 7%. Real traffic sample (anonymized chat workload) shows 26% reduction; further tuning of microstride signature thresholds expected.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature behind runtime flag and console toggle for a small customer cohort.
2) Canary at 1% host traffic for two days with monitoring for latency, OOM, and tail-latency regressions.
3) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% after validation.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for entropy estimator and microstride signature generation.
- Microbench harness for kernel hint paths comparing packed vs dense kernels.
- End-to-end perf job on staging cluster with representative workloads.
- Chaos tests to simulate bursty arrival and worker preemption.

Open design decisions / trade-offs:
- Source of entropy signal: whether to use model-provided token log-probs (more accurate) or cheap proxy from tokenizer frequency tables (faster). Current experiments use model log-probs sampled from a lightweight scorer service; fallback to tokenizer stats is implemented for private deployments without scoring.
- Microstride signature granularity: current 2-bit signature is conservative. Increasing bits improves consolidation but adds state complexity. We will iterate after canary.
- Timeout heuristics: tuned so that latency SLOs are not violated; aggressive consolidation increases padding savings but risks tail latency.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: entropy sampling adds CPU overhead. Mitigation: sample only first 8 tokens and compute using int8-friendly approximations; benchmark shows <0.5% CPU overhead on serving control-plane.
- Risk: incorrect kernel hinting could degrade throughput. Mitigation: conservative thresholds and opt-out per-model metadata.

Notes: this feature dovetails with the KV-cache prefetch scheduled in ENG-20377 and the length harmonizer work in ENG-61437. Work here will contribute kernel affinity metadata to the runtime kernel selector for later use in cross-model routing decisions.
